overview: This is a complaint filed by HydraFacial LLC in Investigation 337-TA-1417 alleging that respondents unlawfully import, sell for importation, and sell within the United States hydrodermabrasion systems (Bela MD, Cleopatra, and MIRApeel) that infringe U.S. Patent Nos. 11,446,477 and 12,053,607, either literally or under the doctrine of equivalents. HydraFacial seeks permanent limited exclusion orders, cease and desist orders, and a bond.

points.point: Hydrodermabrasion systems for skin treatment deliver liquid solutions (containing alpha hydroxy acid, beta hydroxy acid, antioxidants, and moisturizers) to skin using a handpiece tip contacting the patient's skin, with vacuum source drawing solution from a container through the handpiece to the skin and then away for disposal.
points.quote: These hydrodermabrasion systems are configured to deliver various liquid solutions—such as those containing alpha hydroxy acid, beta hydroxy acid, antioxidants, and moisturizers—to the skin of a patient using a handpiece with a tip that contacts the patient's skin

points.point: HydraFacial manufactures the HydraFacial Syndeo system, HydraFacial Elite system, and HydraFacial Allegro system as patented hydrodermabrasion systems, along with tips, accessories, liquid solutions, and boosters for skin treatments.
points.quote: HydraFacial designs, develops, manufactures , and sells other patented hydrodermabrasion systems, including the HydraFacial Elite system and the HydraFacial Allegro system.

points.point: U.S. Patent No. 11,446,477 (the '477 Patent) issued on September 20, 2022, from Application No. 16/517,268 filed July 19, 2019, claiming priority to provisional applications filed December 30, 2005 and February 2, 2006, with expiration date March 29, 2026. HydraFacial owns the entire right, title, and interest by assignment.
points.quote: HydraFacial owns by assignment the entire right, title, and interest in the ' 477 Patent, which duly and lawfully issued on September 20, 2022. The '477 Patent issued from U.S. Patent Application No. 16/517,268, filed July 19, 2019.

points.point: U.S. Patent No. 12,053,607 (the '607 Patent) issued on August 6, 2024, from Application No. 18/487,916 filed October 16, 2023, claiming priority to provisional applications filed December 30, 2005 and February 2, 2006, with expiration date March 29, 2026. HydraFacial owns the entire right, title, and interest by assignment.
points.quote: HydraFacial owns by assignment the entire right, title, and interest in the ' 607 Patent, which duly and lawfully issued on August 6, 2024.

points.point: Asserted claims of the '607 Patent are claims 1, 2-10, 11, 12-13, 15-19, 20 (with claims 1, 11, and 15 being independent claims).
The complaint alleges respondents directly infringe the '477 and '607 Patents, either literally or under the doctrine of equivalents, through the Bela MD, Cleopatra, and MIRApeel systems.
points.quote: Respondents directly infringe, literally or under the doctrine of equivalents, and/or induce or contribute to the infringement of, at least the following claims (collectively, "the Asserted Claims") of the Asserted Patents via the Accused Products

points.point: The complaint alleges respondents induce infringement by recommending, encouraging, instructing, and suggesting customers use the accused products in an infringing manner, and that respondents have knowledge of the asserted patents from cease-and-desist letters sent prior to filing.
points.quote: Respondents also induce the infringement of the Asserted Patents by recommending, encouraging, instructing, and/or suggesting that its customers use the Accused Products in an infringing manner. Respondents have actual knowledge of the Asserted Patents because HydraFacial sent letters to each of t he Respondents prior to filing this Complaint

points.point: The complaint alleges respondents offer for sale and/or sell within the United States, and/or import into the United States, the accused products which constitute material parts of the invention that are not staple articles of commerce suitable for substantial non-infringing use and are known by respondents to be especially made or adapted for use in infringement.
points.quote: Respondents also offer to sell and/or sell within the United States, and/or import into the United States, the Accused Products which constitute material parts of the invention of the Asserted Claims, that are not staple articles or commodities of commerce suitable for substantial non-infringing use

points.point: The Cleopatra system is assembled and manufactured in Germany and/or Poland by MIRAmedtech Germany and/or MIRAmedtech Poland, then imported into the United States, sold for importation, and/or sold after importation by respondents Bio-Infusions and MPR.
points.quote: Upon information and belief, MIRAmedtech Germany, and/or others on MIRAmedtech Germany's behalf, and/or in concert with MIRAmedtech Germany, assemble and manufacture the Cleopatra system in Germany , Poland, or elsewhere outside the United States

points.point: The MIRApeel system is assembled and manufactured in Germany and/or Poland by MIRAmedtech Poland and/or MIRAmedtech Germany, then imported into the United States, sold for importation, and/or sold after importation by respondents eMIRAmed, MIRAmedtech Germany, and MPR.
points.quote: Upon information and belief, MIRAmedtech Poland, and/or others on MIRAmedtech Poland's behalf, and/or in concert with MIRAmedtech Poland, assemble and manufacture the MIRApeel system in Germany, Poland, or elsewhere outside of the United States.

points.point: HydraFacial seeks a permanent limited exclusion order pursuant to Section 337(d) excluding from entry into the United States the Bela MD, Cleopatra, and MIRApeel systems and components that infringe one or more claims of the '477 Patent and/or '607 Patent.

points.point: HydraFacial seeks a bond for the 60-day Presidential review period pursuant to Section 337(j) for the importation of hydrodermabrasion systems and components that infringe one or more claims of the asserted patents.
points.quote: Complainant further seek s as relief a bond, for the 60-day Presidential review period pursuant to Section 337(j), for the importation of certain hydrodermabrasion systems and components thereof that infringe one or more claims of the Asserted Patents.
